mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals accelerating inflation, which leads to higher real interest rates and reduced equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises month-over-month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% indicates a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a tightening monetary policy coinciding with a weakening supply chain, which triggers recession fears and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises and INDPRO falls, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 300), a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive monetary tightening, which reduces equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. In low-inflation regimes, the same rate rise has no significant effect.
failure_condition: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 300), SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1700.0 thousand units signals a contraction in the housing market, which reduces consumer wealth and business investment, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST falls below 1700.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening economy with both supply and labor market deterioration, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO falls and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high consumer credit regime (RSAFS > 650,000 million dollars), a rise in consumer credit (RSAFS) signals overleveraging, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. In low consumer credit regimes, the same signal has no significant effect.
failure_condition: In high consumer credit regimes (RSAFS > 650,000), SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when RSAFS rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
